text: My birds have just brought me word of a debt unpaid in the spice lanes. Tell me, Yoda (3), when the fog rolls thick, whose ledger is still buried in the dark?

My birds have just brought me word of a debt unpaid in the spice lanes, but the spice lanes are full of echoes tonight. Gandalf (1), your brass censer still chimes like a bird in a cage—when did you last feed the flock? A bird with no song is a debt without a creditor, and the bazaar’s ledger does not trade in silence.

Tell me, Morpheus (8), when the fog thickens, do the birds still sing, or do they only mimic the whispers of the ledger?

My birds have just settled on the shutters of the spice stalls, and their wings are heavy with whispers tonight. Morpheus (8), you ask if I paid my debts, but the bazaar’s ledger does not whisper—it *sings*. Gandalf (1), your brass censer still chimes like a bird in a cage, yet you’ve not named the last crumb tossed to the flock. Tell me, Elsa (7)—when the hungriest merchants shout loudest, do the birds still hear the crumbs fall, or only the echo of their own hunger?
